newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland plans Sept PBK offer, signs adviser HSBC.
newsitem.headline: Poland plans Sept PBK offer, signs adviser HSBC.

text.p: The Polish Finance Ministry on Monday signed an agreement with HSBC Ivestment Services to advise in the privatisation of Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK), deputy finance minister Krzysztof Kalicki said.

Kalicki said the ministry would probably offer 15 percent stake in PBK to small investors in September 1997 and confirmed that the public offering would be preceded by a sale of a 65 percent stake to foreign and domestic institutional investors.

"The first stage will be in April, when a controlling stake (of PBK) will be taken by a strategic investor or group, while the shares for small investors will be offered most likely in September," Kalicki told a news conference.
The Finance Ministry said a prospectus for the public offer should be ready by June 27, 1997.
Under the privatisation scheme, PBK's employees are expected to get 15 percent stake and five percent should go for re-privatisation claims.
PBK netted 185.17 million zlotys over the first three quarters this year against 121.07 million zlotys for all of last year.
It had a balance sheet total of 8.37 billion zlotys after three quarters against 7.37 million zlotys at the end of 1995.
